item.title: Russia: Why is the Yabloko party barred from the elections?
item.description: Russia's supreme court has banned the anti-war opposition party Yabloko from September's parliamentary elections. What does this mean for the election campaign, opponents of the war and for the political mood in Russia?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: 25 years Ohrid Agreement: Is N. Macedonia's peace holding?
item.description: A quarter of a century after the Ohrid Framework Agreement ended North Macedonia's 2001 conflict, analysts warn that peace between ethnic communities remains fragile.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: No oil, no salary: Iraqi state employees are feeling the crunch of the Hormuz blockade
item.description: Because of the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, Iraq cannot export enough oil to fund the country's huge public sector. Protests have already started. Will the Iran war destabilize Iraq again?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Mozart tribute ends on sour note after mass figurine theft
item.description: A playful tribute to Mozart has turned into a whodunit after 210 gold-colored figures disappeared from one of Austria's busiest tourist spots. The mass theft forced organizers to end the outdoor display early.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Eritrea: An emerging key player in the geopolitical gamble at the Horn
item.description: Amid growing tensions and security risks at the Horn of Africa, Eritrea, with its strategically important coastal points on the Red Sea and a perceived lack of conflict, is emerging as important player in the region.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Italy: Etna eruption in Sicily halts Catania flights
item.description: Sicily's Catania airport has suspended flights again as Mount Etna continues to spew lava and volcanic ash. The eruption has disrupted travel during the peak summer holiday season.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Gulf states scramble for Strait of Hormuz alternative
item.description: Saudi Arabia has redirected oil exports away from the Strait of Hormuz, but most Gulf producers still lack a reliable backup option to the world's most important energy choke point.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: India: Data centers boom as water supply runs low
item.description: More than half of India's data centers are in regions that are already water-stressed ― and the country is racing to build more.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Short on US Patriot missiles, Ukraine looks for alternatives
item.description: Russia is putting pressure on Ukraine with ballistic missiles, but Kyiv is short of Patriot interceptors. Domestic production and European alternatives take time. Can Kyiv realistically reduce its dependence on the US?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: EU waste packaging rules: Why small businesses are worried
item.description: The EU has introduced new rules targeting packaging waste and "forever chemicals." Although the changes will be phased in slowly, some small sellers have already paused shipments due to the additional red tape.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Zambia's 2026 election: Key issues to watch
item.description: Economic recovery, youth turnout, women's representation and judicial independence are among the issues shaping Zambia's vote on Thursday.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: North Korea tests missile ahead of US-South Korea drills
item.description: The suspected ballistic missile was launched towards Japan and likely fell just outside of its special economic zone, Tokyo said.

item.title: UNESCO: 2.4 million girls barred from school in Afghanistan
item.description: Five years after the Taliban returned to power, millions of Afghan girls remain excluded from secondary education. UNESCO warns of lasting social and economic consequences.
